works.abstract: Underwater marine debris poses significant threats to marine ecosystems and coastal environments, yet remains largely invisible to traditional satellite-based monitoring systems. We present Neural Oceans, a forecasting system for predicting underwater debris accumulation patterns using physics-informed deep learning. Our two-phase methodology combines Lagrangian particle simulation driven by real oceanographic data with a convolutional neural network - long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) architecture for spatiotemporal prediction. We generate training data through a realistic particle transport simulation incorporating 157,550 underwater debris particles released at SeaClear H2020 survey sites across the Mediterranean Sea. Our physics-informed feature engineering creates 17 hydrodynamic variables capturing multi-scale transport processes. The CNN-LSTM model processes 7-day environmental sequences to predict debris density fields 36 hours ahead with uncertainty quantification. Evaluation on 172 training sequences demonstrates an R2value equal to 0.623, a correlation of 0.791, and a hotspot F1-score equal to 0.710. The 72 × 325 spatial resolution enables regional marine management applications while remaining computationally tractable for real-time deployment. Neural Oceans addresses critical gaps in marine debris monitoring by providing forecasting capability with practical lead times for cleanup prioritization, survey optimization, and marine protected area management.
works.journal: International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications
works.title: Neural Oceans: Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Underwater Marine Debris Forecasting
